subject.title: [Feature]: When building a work system with OpenClaw as the core, WebUI should remain accessible after the Gateway crashes.

question: Should OpenClaw core own a crash-survivor same-port Control UI fallback after the Gateway process exits, or should this remain a deployment supervisor/reverse-proxy pattern?
rationale: The requested behavior crosses process supervision, public config, and Control UI security boundaries; code inspection shows it cannot be satisfied by a simple in-process Gateway toggle.

options.title: Document supervisor pattern
options.body: Keep core lean and document systemd/reverse-proxy recovery as the supported enterprise deployment pattern unless a concrete core API gap is identified.

options.title: Sponsor core rescue sidecar
options.body: Accept the new core availability surface and design a narrow supervised static sidecar with explicit auth, TLS, origin, port handoff, and upgrade tests.

options.title: Decline native fallback
options.body: Close the direction as out of scope for OpenClaw core and ask operators to use existing process supervisors or infrastructure tooling.

recommendation.title: Document supervisor pattern
recommendation.body: Keep core lean and document systemd/reverse-proxy recovery as the supported enterprise deployment pattern unless a concrete core API gap is identified.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision sits on the Gateway/Control UI architecture and feature history that steipete originally introduced and has most heavily maintained.
